headline_stat.name: Estimated BF range across 4 synthetic neurons

stated_limitation: Synthetic data generation uses simplified neural models; actual STRFs may show more complex structure

justification.dataset: Dandiset 000006 is named but never loaded; the analysis runs entirely on self-generated synthetic data, so no real dataset containing the phenomenon was used.
justification.handling: No real data was streamed or loaded at all; the stimulus and spikes are fabricated in code, an automatic 0.
justification.analysis: Ridge-regression reverse correlation is a defensible STRF method in principle, but here it only tries to recover a made-up ground truth and does not test the phenomenon in real recordings.
justification.correctness: Numbers reproduce from the seeded code but the synthetic recovery is internally inconsistent (two distinct nominal BFs both estimate to 9611 Hz, two neurons at 0% variance) while being presented as clean population tuning.
justification.figures: Figures are labeled and readable but the STRF heatmaps are noisy with a degenerate 2-bin temporal axis and 0% variance panels presented as receptive fields.
justification.honesty: Although the synthetic nature is disclosed, the write-up presents failed recovery (0% variance, mismatched BFs) and draws biological conclusions about tonotopy and latency as if the analysis supported them, overstating what a made-up dataset can show.
